code.title: Pointer Value Viewer
code.description:
A lab assistant stores a reading and inspects it through a pointer. Read one integer, store its address in a pointer, then print the value seen through the pointer and the doubled value obtained by dereferencing the same pointer.

Input Format:
One line with one integer n.

Output Format:
Via pointer: <n>
Doubled: <2 * n>

Constraints:
-1000 <= n <= 1000

code.title: Swap Two Integers via Pointers
code.description:
A delivery desk stores two parcel weights on two shelves and swaps them using only pointers. Read two integers, swap their values purely by dereferencing pointers to them, and print both values after the swap.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b.

Output Format:
First after swap: <b>
Second after swap: <a>

Constraints:
-1000 <= a, b <= 1000
code.output1:
First after swap: 5
Second after swap: 5
code.output2:
First after swap: 9
Second after swap: -4
code.output3:
First after swap: -100
Second after swap: 100
code.sampleoutput1:
First after swap: 8
Second after swap: 3
code.sampleoutput2:
First after swap: 20
Second after swap: 10

code.title: Larger Value via Pointer Function
code.description:
A referee records two innings scores and wants the bigger one reported through a pointer. Read two integers. A function receives the addresses of the two integers, compares the values it finds there, and returns the pointer to the larger value. Print the value through that returned pointer.

Input Format:
One line with two integers s1 and s2.

Output Format:
Larger: <larger value>

Constraints:
-10000 <= s1, s2 <= 10000

code.title: Tally Raised Through a Pointer
code.description:
An event desk keeps a head-count tally in one int. Read the starting count, point a pointer at it, and increase the count exactly five times using the dereference-and-increment form (*p)++ inside a loop. Print the final tally through the pointer.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: the starting count.

Output Format:
Final tally: <count + 5>

Constraints:
-100 <= starting count <= 100000

code.title: Array Tour with a Moving Pointer
code.description:
A projector operator walks through a slide deck using a pointer. Read N integers into an array, then traverse it with a pointer using p++ and *(p + i), printing all values on one line separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Values: <v1> <v2> ... <vN>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000 <= each value <= 1000

code.title: Sum Through a Pointer
code.description:
A cashier totals a row of amounts by walking a pointer across them. Read N integers into an array, compute the sum using only a pointer (never indexing the array with brackets) and print the total.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Total: <sum>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -5000 <= each value <= 5000

code.title: Sensor Calibrator
code.description:
A weather station calibrates raw sensor readings: any reading strictly below the threshold is doubled to amplify the weak signal, and readings at or above the threshold stay unchanged. Read N readings into a heap array created with new, walk a pointer through the array applying the rule, print the calibrated list, then release the memory with delete[].

Input Format:
First line: N and threshold (two integers).
Second line: N integer readings.

Output Format:
Calibrated: <list of N values separated by single spaces>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -100 <= threshold <= 100, -100 <= each reading <= 100

code.title: Scoreboard Updater
code.description:
A quiz scoreboard adds a fixed bonus to every player's score. Read N scores and a bonus, walk a pointer across the scores adding the bonus to each one through the pointer, then print the updated list and the team total.

Input Format:
First line: N and bonus (two integers).
Second line: N scores.

Output Format:
Updated: <list of updated scores>
Team total: <sum of updated scores>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 0 <= bonus <= 50, 0 <= each score <= 200

code.title: Inventory Restocker
code.description:
A warehouse supervisor scans shelf stock counts; any item whose count has dropped to zero is immediately restocked to a default quantity. Read N counts and a default quantity, walk a pointer across the counts replacing every zero with the default through the pointer, then print the final list and how many items were restocked.

Input Format:
First line: N and defaultQty (two integers).
Second line: N stock counts.

Output Format:
Stock: <list of final counts>
Restocked: <number of zeros replaced>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 1 <= defaultQty <= 500, 0 <= each count <= 500

code.title: Taxi Fare Reducer
code.description:
A cab company announces a flat 10 percent discount on every fare in its log. Read N fares, walk a pointer across them replacing each fare with 90 percent of itself through the pointer, then print the discounted fares with exactly two decimal places each.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N fares.

Output Format:
Discounted: <f1> <f2> ... <fN> (each with exactly 2 decimals)

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 0 <= each fare <= 10000

code.title: Peak Reading Index Hunt
code.description:
A quality inspector records N test readings and needs the position of the highest one. Walk a pointer across the array keeping a second pointer on the best value seen so far, then report the maximum value and the 0-based index where it first occurs.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Max value: <v>
Max index: <i>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each value <= 10000

code.title: Two-Pointer Array Reverser
code.description:
A photo editor flips a strip of color codes. Read N integers, then reverse the array in place using two pointers — one starting at the first element and one at the last — swapping the values they point at while the pointers move toward each other. Print the reversed list.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Reversed: <list of N values separated by single spaces>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each value <= 10000

code.title: Heap Clone Cartridge
code.description:
A game console clones a level's coin layout into fresh heap memory. Read N integers into a local array, allocate a second array of the same size with new, copy the values using only pointer arithmetic (two moving pointers, no bracket indexing), print both lists, then release the heap copy with delete[].

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Original: <list of N values>
Clone: <list of N values>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 500, -1000 <= each value <= 1000

code.title: Code Word Replacer
code.description:
A firmware engineer patches a register log: every occurrence of an old code is replaced with a new code. Read N integers, then an old code and a new code. Walk a pointer across the array replacing every match through the pointer, then print how many replacements were made and the final list.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.
Third line: old code and new code (two integers).

Output Format:
Replaced: <count>
Updated: <list of N values>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -100 <= each value and code <= 100

code.title: Min Max Single Sweep
code.description:
A stock auditor checks one shelf in a single sweep. Read N integers and, using exactly one pointer pass (no second scan), find the smallest and largest values together with the 0-based index where each first occurs. Print both results.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Min: <v> at index <i>
Max: <v> at index <i>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each value <= 10000
code.output1:
Min: -3 at index 0
Max: -3 at index 0
code.output2:
Min: 1 at index 2
Max: 9 at index 0
code.output3:
Min: -6 at index 3
Max: 5 at index 2
code.sampleoutput1:
Min: 2 at index 2
Max: 9 at index 4
code.sampleoutput2:
Min: 5 at index 0
Max: 5 at index 0

code.title: Dynamic Array Grow Room
code.description:
A playlist app doubles its storage when new songs arrive. Read N values and a pad value. Store the original N values in a local array, then allocate a new heap array of size 2N with new; copy the original values into it using pointer arithmetic, fill the remaining N slots with the pad value, print both lists, and release the heap array with delete[].

Input Format:
First line: N and pad (two integers).
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Original: <list of N values>
Grown: <N values followed by N pad values>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 500, -1000 <= pad <= 1000, -1000 <= each value <= 1000

code.title: Memory Pool Manager
code.description:
A tiny embedded device manages a pool of one-int memory blocks. It reads N and then N values, allocating one heap block per value with new and remembering each block's address. Then it releases every alternate block starting from block 0 (indices 0, 2, 4, ...) using delete, setting each released pointer to nullptr so no dangling pointer remains. Finally it prints the state of every block: released blocks print -1, live blocks print their stored value read through the non-null pointer. Before exiting, every remaining live block is deleted as well.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
N lines, line i being:
Block <i>: <value or -1>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 0 <= each value <= 1000

code.title: Stack on the Heap
code.description:
A text editor keeps its undo history on a stack built over a heap array, using a pure pointer as the top marker (top points one slot past the top element). Read the number of commands C, then C commands, one per line: push x, pop, or peek. The stack starts empty. Every pop prints the removed value and every peek prints the top value, each on its own line; a pop or peek on an empty stack prints UNDERFLOW. After all commands, print the values still on the stack from top to bottom on one line prefixed with Stack from top:, or Stack from top: EMPTY when nothing remains. Release the heap array before exiting.

Input Format:
First line: one integer C.
Next C lines: one command each.

Output Format:
One line per pop/peek result, then the final stack line.

Constraints:
1 <= C <= 200, -1000 <= x <= 1000
code.sampleinput1:
6
push 4
push 9
pop
peek
push 2
pop
code.input3:
7
push 5
pop
pop
push -8
push 12
peek
pop

code.title: Matrix Row Swapper
code.description:
A seating chart grid stores marks in R rows and C columns held in one heap block. The coordinator swaps two rows. Read R and C, then the 0-based row indices i and j to swap, then the R*C values row by row. Swap rows i and j by walking two row pointers through the heap block, then print the resulting matrix. Release the heap block before exiting.

Input Format:
First line: R and C (two integers).
Second line: i and j (two integers, 0-based).
Next R lines: C integers each.

Output Format:
R lines after the swap, each with C values separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 20, 0 <= i, j < R, -1000 <= each value <= 1000

code.title: Sliding Window Pointer Scanner
code.description:
A network monitor scans traffic counts with a sliding window. Read N and the window size W, then N integers. Slide two pointers across the data: add the entering element through the front pointer and drop the leaving element through the rear pointer, printing the sum of every window as it forms. Finally print the maximum window sum seen.

Input Format:
First line: N and W (two integers, W <= N).
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Window sums: <s1> <s2> ... <s_last>
Max window sum: <m>

Constraints:
1 <= W <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each value <= 10000

mcqs.title: Why delete Pairs with new

mcqs.Option1: To make the program run faster
mcqs.Option2: Because new can only be called once per program
mcqs.Option3: To convert heap memory into stack memory
mcqs.Option4: To return heap memory to the system and avoid memory leaks

mcqs.description: What happens when a running program dereferences a pointer whose value is nullptr?
mcqs.Option3: It is undefined behaviour and typically crashes

mcqs.title: What a Memory Leak Is
mcqs.description: A memory leak occurs when:
mcqs.Option1: A pointer is declared without initialization
mcqs.Option2: Stack memory runs out during recursion
mcqs.Option3: Heap memory allocated with new is never freed and can no longer be reached
mcqs.Option4: Two pointers hold the same address

mcqs.title: What new Returns
mcqs.description: The expression new int in C++:
mcqs.Option1: Returns the address of one int allocated on the heap
mcqs.Option2: Returns the value of a brand new int
mcqs.Option3: Returns an int initialised to zero
mcqs.Option4: Returns the address of an int on the stack
